name: Feeding America
mission: Our mission is to advance change in America by ensuring fair access to nutritious food for all in partnership with food banks, policymakers, supporters, and the communities we serve.
theoryOfChange: In partnership with subject matter experts, practitioners, and member food banks, Feeding America evaluates programs, interventions, and strategies that address food insecurity and diet-related chronic disease. By leveraging the strength of the food bank network, Feeding America has the opportunity to disseminate best practices that facilitate continuous learning and improvement of programs and build evidence of improved life outcomes for the people we serve.

strengths_deep_dive: Feeding America's primary strength lies in its ability to convert corporate food waste into community relief at an industrial scale. By securing <cite id="5">2,347,000,000 pounds of donated food product</cite> in a single fiscal year, the organization acts as the central nervous system for domestic hunger relief. This efficiency is reflected in its <cite id="1">100/100 Impact & Measurement beacon score</cite>, which validates the direct link between its activities and its mission. Furthermore, the organization serves as a major funder for local communities, awarding <cite id="5">$195,221,000 in member grants</cite> in FY2024 to support regional food bank infrastructure.
rich_narrative.summary: Feeding America operates as a massive domestic hunger-relief organization, functioning as a nationwide network of food banks and advocacy programs. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="7">total revenue of $5,047,685,550</cite>, reflecting its significant scale in the American nonprofit landscape. The organization maintains a <cite id="1">96/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, which indicates a high level of institutional stability and public trust. Its operations are characterized by a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 98.3%</cite>, meaning that the value of food distributed and program services matches or exceeds its total cash and non-cash revenue. A critical component of this financial structure is the high volume of non-cash contributions; approximately <cite id="1">97% of revenue is non-cash contributions</cite>, primarily in the form of donated food products. This model allows the charity to achieve <cite id="1">fundraising efficiency of $0.01 per $1 raised</cite>, as it leverages massive corporate donations to feed millions. Beyond direct distribution, the organization engages in <cite id="14">policy and advocacy, research, and food rescue</cite> to address the root causes of food insecurity. While the scale is impressive, the organization maintains <cite id="1">1.4 months of working capital in working capital</cite>, which is relatively lean for an institution of this size. For donors, this represents a highly efficient vehicle for domestic food security, though the heavy reliance on Gift-in-Kind (GIK) food donations means cash contributions are often used to facilitate the logistics and grants required to move that food through the network.
